subject: IonCommerce SLO / Throughput snapshot & proposed sizing
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@ioncommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: IonCommerce SLO / Throughput snapshot & proposed sizing

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the next steps so we have a shared picture.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: interactive order-assist chat on IonCommerce checkout (widget embedded on product pages).
- Typical session length: 1–6 turns, avg 220 tokens per turn, median ~180 tokens.
- Current baseline traffic: 70 QPS during business hours (checkout page impressions), peak spikes observed during promotions up to ~420 QPS for short windows (~3–8 minutes).
- Streaming: client expects chunked/streaming responses (SSE) to display partial suggestions as tokens arrive. p50 latency target for first token: <=120ms; p99 end-to-end generation target: <=350ms for non-streaming completion.
- Concurrency: concurrent open sessions ~1.2x QPS (accounting for streaming window), expected growth x2 in next 6 months.

Attached: ioncom_workload_snapshot.csv (sample traffic distribution + token histogram).

Proposed immediate asks / next steps:
1) Alex: please confirm whether the 420 QPS spikes are global or concentrated in a single region and whether they are predictable (marketing campaigns).
2) IonCommerce: share a single-day logs export (already attached partial sample) showing per-minute QPS and a 95th/99th token length distribution.
3) Redwood (Rishi / Marissa): we will produce a quick-sizing note with two options: a) hosted pilot (burst-tolerant) that uses smart routing + autoscaling and b) reserved Dedicated pool for predictable latency at peak. Estimate delivery: EOD 2026-07-13.

I looped in Marissa for the implementation checklist and Rishi for commercial alignment.

Thanks — Neha

--

From: Alex Wong <alex.wong@ioncommerce.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@ioncommerce.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IonCommerce SLO / Throughput snapshot & proposed sizing

Thanks Neha — short clarifications below. Appreciate the rapid follow-up.

Answers to your asks:
- Spikes: the 420 QPS peaks are mostly regional (US-East) and tied to our flash promotions. They last ~3–7 minutes and are somewhat predictable (we have a campaign calendar).
- Token distribution: median tokens per request ~180 as you noted, 95th ~420, 99th ~900 (rare long contextual requests).
- Streaming: yes, SSE for partial responses is required for UX. We display partial suggestions after ~50 tokens.
- SLA expectations: our engineering org wants p50 first-byte <= 120ms and p99 completion <= 300–350ms (we can tolerate slightly higher p99 for the 99th token-length tail if we use a fallback shorter-context path).
- Risk tolerance: high sensitivity to latency during checkout; we prefer predictable latency even if it costs a bit more.

I'm attaching the one-day logs export (partial) and a simple promo calendar. Let us know if you need additional percentiles.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product — Checkout
IonCommerce

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IonCommerce SLO / Throughput snapshot & proposed sizing (internal)

Looping internal ops for a quick sanity check before we send numbers to Alex. High level thoughts:
- Workload shape: steady baseline ~70 QPS with short-duration ~6x crests to 420 QPS. This pattern favors an architecture that can tolerate bursts without pre-provisioning full peak when the peaks are short and somewhat predictable.
- Streaming requirement (SSE) increases concurrency and memory pressure due to open keep-alive connections; we should model concurrent open streams as roughly 1.2x the QPS for slot calculations.
- Token tail (99th ~900) matters for buffer sizing and KV-cache usage; recommend two-tier model: standard context path (up to 512 tokens) and long-tail path (quantized model / longer latency tolerance).

Questions for Marissa / infra:
1) Based on our kernel/quantization options, can we meet p50 first-byte <=120ms for the standard path at 70 QPS steady and p99 <=350ms given a single Dedicated node configuration? If not, what dedicated capacity would be needed?
2) Can autoscaling warm pools be fast enough to absorb a 6x spike within 90s if we use hosted + smart routing?

If Marissa confirms we can hit the standard-path SLOs at modest dedicated capacity, I'll propose 2 configs for Alex: (A) hosted pilot with burst buffer and warm standby (cost-optimized) and (B) dedicated 2-node pool (latency-optimized). Neha, I can draft the sizing table by EOD.

-Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra | Solutions Lead, Go-to-market

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@ioncommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: IonCommerce SLO / Throughput snapshot & proposed sizing

Alex — thanks for the data. Following internal validation, below is our recommended immediate plan and a sizing estimate for the pilot.

Executive summary (pilot):
- Approach: 6-week hosted pilot using Redwood hosted API with warm-standby autoscaling + prefix caching for repeated prompts. If pilot meets latency SLOs, transition to Dedicated reserved capacity before Q4 traffic events.
- Why hosted first: faster time-to-value, easier to iterate on prompt/context window sizing and streaming integration. We will use smart routing to a quantized long-tail path for requests >512 tokens to avoid p99 blowups.

Sizing estimate (baseline assumptions: avg turn 220 tokens, median 180, steady QPS 70, peak short-window 420 QPS):
- Standard path (<=512 tokens): 70 steady QPS => equivalent token/sec ~15,400 tps (70 * 220). Include concurrency multiplier 1.2 => slot planning for ~84 concurrent streams. To meet p50 first-token <=120ms on standard path, our bench suggests 1 dedicated high-efficiency GPU equivalent per 200 steady QPS if using quantized 4-bit kernels; for pilot hosted we will emulate with reserved warm pool of 2 warm workers to absorb bursts.
- Peak handling: for short 6x peaks, recommend warm-standby capacity + 4 burst workers in hosted to cap cold-start latency. If guaranteed dedicated: 2-node pool (NVIDIA A10/A30 class) should give headroom for steady+short peaks with p99 ~300–350ms on standard path.
- Long-tail (>512 tokens): route to quantized long-path nodes; expect 2x latency on p99 but keep p50 acceptable.

Attachments: draft SLA and a short sizing table (sla-draft-ioncom-v1.docx).

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm region targeting (US-East confirmed?) and approve pilot start window (we can kick off onboarding week of 2026-07-20).
2) IonCommerce: sign the pilot SOW (I attached a redline-ready doc).
3) Redwood: Rishi & Marissa will produce an itemized pilot runbook and a cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated by EOD 2026-07-14.

If that aligns, I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff to iron out integration points (SSE implementation, auth keys, and telemetry hooks).

Thanks — Neha
